text:
toni_sales: Quick thread for the MercuryBank POC ask. They sent a checklist: BYO-CMK via customer HSMs (CloudHSM or Thales Luna), keys in EU+US, FIPS 140-2 L3 attestation required, rotation cadence 30 days (may request 14 days for some workloads), immediate revoke with <15min RTO, audit retention 10 years, traffic profile ~2.5k req/s steady with 5k/s peak bursts. POC goal: 6 weeks. Need technical + commercial callouts.

leo_se: We can integrate both CloudHSM and Thales via our KMS-proxy. Mode: envelope encryption where Redwood stores wrapped DEKs only. Important: Thales on-prem will require an IP allowlist and a short-lived VPN or transit link for connector.

emily_sec: Security notes: we do not import raw key material. For Thales/CloudHSM we use HSM-backed CMKs and request vendor attestation (cert chain). For FIPS L3 we need their attestation artifact before go-live. Audit logs: JSON schema includes timestamp, key_fingerprint, operation, actor, src_ip, request_id, hsm_attestation_b64. We can push logs to their S3 with server-side encryption. 10-year retention OK if they manage lifecycle on their bucket.

michael_cust: Confirming: MercuryBank insists on key ceremony windows during CET business hours and wants Redwood to run a simulated ceremony for DR. Also they want an option for Redwood to hold an encrypted escrow under a dual-control process for emergencies.

toni_sales: Can we commit to simulated ceremony and escrow option as a paid add-on?

rick_fin: Pricing rough: Dedicated baseline $14k/mo. BYO-HSM connector setup + attestation handling $6k/mo. High-throughput surcharge for 2.5k steady /5k burst: $4k/mo. Escrow (encrypted, multi-signer manual retrieval) add-on: $2.5k/mo + one-time key-ceremony support $15k. POC professional services: $30k estimate. Suggest 6-week paid POC at 75% monthly rate to reserve capacity and priority.

leo_se: Engineering callouts / risks: 1) Throughput: decrypt-heavy workloads spike latency; need to know encrypt/decrypt ratio. 2) Cache invalidation: we push invalidations but pre-warmed KV caches may persist until TTL; for strict revocation set TTL low. 3) Atomic rotation: we support staged rollout (new DEK + dual-write) to avoid in-flight failures. 4) On-prem HSMs require peered VPC or VPN and static egress IPs from our connector.

emily_sec: Revocation detail: forced revoke triggers cache invalidation + immediate KMS deny list. Measured end-to-end ~10-20s in high-throughput tests, but if they have aggressive batching windows it can be longer. We will document the tradeoffs and recommend a short TTL during the POC for critical routes.

zara_ops: Ops / runbook: propose 6-week plan: Week1: network & certs, Week2: connector deploy + handshake, Week3: integrate envelope calls + rotation hook, Week4: functional & chaos tests (simulate HSM failover), Week5: load tests to validate 2.5k steady/5k burst, Week6: ceremony rehearsal + runbook handoff. I'll attach runbook checklist after triage.

toni_sales: Any legal constraints re escrow? MercuryBank legal insists escrow retrieval requires 2 Redwood approvers + 2 bank approvers and retrieval windows only in declared emergencies. Can Security draft language?

emily_sec: Yes, we can add an escrow addendum with dual-controller retrieval and audit logging. We'll also add explicit language that Redwood does not have access to plaintext key material and escrowed blobs remain encrypted with customer KEK.

devops_bot: POC ticket created: POC-4990 assigned to leo_se and zara_ops. See https://redwood.internal/pocs/POC-4990

toni_sales: Action items:
- leo_se: produce integration checklist & sample connector config (by Tue)
- zara_ops: create POC runbook & load test plan (by Wed)
- rick_fin: draft POC commercial (6-week pricing + escrow add-on) (by Tue)
- emily_sec: prepare security addendum + sample audit schema (48h)
- michael_cust: confirm HSM vendor (CloudHSM vs Thales), decrypt/encrypt ratio, and whether they will provide peered VPC or want Redwood connectors in their network (by Mon)

ton i_sales: thanks — let's sync on a customer call Wed. :thumbsup:
